comparisons.peer_topic: Scope of Global Regulatory Compliance and Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's global operations are subject to a wide range of US and foreign laws, including those governing export control, data privacy, and AI. While current compliance has not materially impacted financial results, future regulatory changes or failure to comply could materially adversely affect capital expenditures, operations, competitive position, and expose the company to fines, sales limits, and reputational damage.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose that their global operations are subject to a wide range of evolving U.S. and foreign laws and regulations. AVGO broadly states that these laws are central to its business and their applicability remains uncertain. AMD provides a more specific list of regulatory areas (e.g., export control, data privacy, AI, environmental) and explicitly contrasts current compliance impacts (not material) with potential future adverse impacts on capital expenditures and competitive position if regulations change or compliance fails.

sentences.text: We are subject to numerous regulations and laws in the United States and abroad involving matters central to our business.
Many of these laws and regulations are evolving and their applicability and scope, as interpreted by the courts, remain uncertain.

Our global operations are subject to various United States and foreign laws and regulations, including, but not limited to, those relating to export control, customs, intellectual property, data privacy and security, climate, environmental, health and safety requirements, cybersecurity, tax, employment, competition and anti-trust, anti-corruption, anti-bribery, conflict minerals, corporate governance, financial and other disclosures, and AI.
However, compliance with changes to existing or new regulations may have a material adverse impact on our future capital expenditures, results of operations or competitive position.

In addition, the failure to comply with government laws and regulations may subject us to consequences including fines, limits on our ability to sell our products, suspension of certain of our business activities, reputational damage, criminal and civil liabilities, and sanctions, which may have a material adverse effect on our capital expenditures, results of operations or competitive position.

comparisons.peer_topic: Government incentives and CHIPS Act funding agreements
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel works with governments to obtain incentives for semiconductor R&D and manufacturing to offset higher regional costs and support a balanced supply chain. In 2024, Intel signed agreements for up to $7.9 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS Act commercial program and up to $3 billion under the Secure Enclave program, and expects benefits from the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit.
comparisons.comparison: While AVGO focuses on general regulatory compliance and uncertainty, INTC's disclosed candidate focuses specifically on government incentives and funding agreements (CHIPS Act). Both disclosures relate to the intersection of government policy and semiconductor operations, but INTC highlights active engagement to secure financial support and offset costs, whereas AVGO highlights the risks and uncertainties of adhering to existing complex regulations.
